title: Funnels and flows
summary: How to build honest sweeps funnels that earn: choosing a funnel shape, prelanders, quizzes, entry forms, DOI confirmation and the tracking that ties them together. Every step is judged on accepted EPC, with starting rules for when to keep, fix or drop it.

lessons.title: Funnel shapes for sweeps and lead gen
objectives: By the end you can describe the five common sweeps funnel shapes and when each fits.
By the end you can compare funnel shapes by accepted EPC, not form rate.
By the end you can plan a fair test between two funnel shapes.

steps.p: The same ad and offer can earn very different amounts depending on what sits between the click and the form. A funnel that adds one honest page can lift accepted EPC; one that adds a misleading page can double leads and halve payouts. The shape is a money decision.

d.b: The page between the click and the form is where you earn
d.s: Pick the shape on accepted EPC, not on lead count.

steps.say: Here's why funnel shape matters. The same ad and offer can earn very different amounts depending on what sits between the click and the form. A funnel that adds one honest page can lift accepted E P C, earnings per click. One that adds a misleading page can double leads and halve payouts. As the screen says, the page between the click and the form is where you earn. Pick the shape on accepted E P C, not on lead count.

steps.p: This is the full flow you will build across this module. Every arrow is a place people drop off or data can break. The postback at the end is how you learn which ads made money.
steps.say: This map shows a complete sweeps flow, the one you'll build across this module. Follow the arrows. The ad sends a click to your tracker, which redirects to a prelander. From there people enter on the entry form, then confirm through a D O I email, double opt-in. That goes to the network, which fires a postback that reports back to your tracker. Every arrow is a place people drop off or data can break. The postback is how you learn which ads made money.

steps.p: Most sweeps campaigns use one of these. Not every offer allows every shape: some forbid prelanders, many forbid platform lead forms. Check the offer terms before you plan.
d: Direct link|ad straight to the entry form
Prelander|one honest page that explains the draw
Quiz|a few light questions, then the entry
Multi-step|ZIP or email first, details next
Platform lead form|form inside the ad app
steps.say: Most sweeps campaigns use one of these five shapes. Direct link sends the ad straight to the entry form. A prelander is one honest page that explains the draw. A quiz asks a few light questions, then leads to the entry. Multi-step asks for a zip code or email first, then details next. And a platform lead form puts the form inside the ad app. Not every offer allows every shape. Some forbid prelanders, and many forbid platform lead forms. Check the offer terms first.

steps.p: A rough guide, not a law. Your traffic, geo and offer decide what works, so treat this table as where to start testing, not as the answer. Your own accepted EPC is the only answer.
steps.say: Here's a rough guide to when each shape fits. Direct link is simple and fast, but watch for low intent and more scrubs. A prelander explains and filters, but it's an extra page, so speed matters. A quiz is engaging, but watch for misleading results. Multi-step has an easy first step, but must not imply eligibility. A lead form has a high form rate, but lower quality and data rules. Treat this table as where to start testing. Your own accepted E P C is the only real answer.

steps.p: Example. Direct: 1,000 clicks, 15% fill the form, 150 leads. Prelander: 64% click through to the form and 28% of those enter, 179 leads. People who read the prelander knew what they entered, so more are accepted.
steps.say: Here's an example comparing a direct link with a prelander. Direct: one thousand clicks, fifteen percent fill the form, one hundred and fifty leads. Now follow the prelander funnel on screen. Six hundred and forty reach the form, one hundred and seventy nine become leads, and one hundred and fifty seven are paid, eighty eight percent. People who read the prelander knew what they were entering, so more of their leads are accepted.

steps.p: Same traffic and a $1.20 SOI. Direct: 150 leads × 85% × $1.20 = $153, EPC $0.15. Prelander: 157 paid × $1.20 = $188.40, EPC $0.19. Quiz: about $0.19. Lead form: 300 leads × 50% × $1.20 = $180, EPC $0.18.
steps.more: Example only. The lead form shows the trap: it doubled leads, but half were rejected because people tapped through a pre-filled form without reading. Your numbers will differ. The method does not: compare shapes on accepted earnings per click.
steps.say: Now compare accepted E P C by shape, with the same traffic and a one dollar twenty S O I, single opt-in, payout. Look at the bars. Direct link earns fifteen cents per click. Prelander and quiz each earn about nineteen cents. The lead form earns eighteen cents, if allowed. Notice the trap in the lead form. It doubled leads, but half were rejected, because people tapped through a pre-filled form without reading. This is an example, so your numbers will differ. The method doesn't: compare on accepted earnings per click.

steps.p: Example prelander funnel from this lesson. Work out each step's pass-through rate from the step above, then enter the index of the weakest one (first row = 0). That step is where to focus your next test.
steps.more: Clicks to form: 64%. Form to lead: 179 ÷ 640 = 28%. Lead to paid: 157 ÷ 179 = 88%. The form step, index 2, loses the largest share. That points at the offer's form or at visitors arriving unsure what they are entering.

d.task: Which step has the lowest pass-through rate from the step above? Enter its index (first row = 0).

steps.say: Time for a lab, using the prelander funnel from this lesson. Work out each step's pass-through rate from the step above it. Then enter the index of the weakest step, where the first row, clicks, is zero. That weakest step is where to focus your next test. Pause and try it, then check your answer.

steps.p: Multi-step flows ask for one easy field first. Honest versions say which step this is, what comes next and who can enter. They never suggest the person has qualified for anything by typing a ZIP code.

page.p: Enter your email to start your entry in the June $500 draw. Next: confirm by email. Free, US 18+. Rules below.

steps.say: Multi-step flows ask for one easy field first. Look at this example on the phone. The heading says step one of two, your email. The text explains you're starting your entry in the June five hundred dollar draw, that the next step is to confirm by email, that it's free for U S adults eighteen plus, and that rules are below. That's the honest version. It says which step this is, what comes next and who can enter. It never suggests someone has qualified just by typing a zip code.

steps.p: Use these steps for each new offer. They take a few minutes and stop you building a funnel the offer does not allow, or a test that cannot give you a clear answer. Tap through each step.

steps.title: Read the offer's funnel rules
steps.text: Look for 'prelanders allowed', 'lead forms allowed' and approved pages.

steps.title: Pick a baseline
steps.text: Start with the simplest allowed shape that explains the draw. Usually a prelander.

steps.title: Plan the split
steps.text: Same ad, same audience, traffic split evenly by your tracker.

steps.title: Set the read point
steps.text: Decide now: compare after 500+ clicks per path on accepted EPC.

steps.say: Here's how to choose your first shape for each new offer. Tap Next to follow each step. First, read the offer's funnel rules. In this example, prelanders are allowed, but platform lead forms are not. Second, pick a baseline, the simplest allowed shape that explains the draw, usually a prelander. Here the challenger is a direct link. Third, plan the split: same ad, same audience, traffic split evenly by your tracker, fifty fifty. Fourth, set the read point now: compare after five hundred or more clicks per path, on accepted E P C.

steps.p: These mistakes come from looking at the wrong number or skipping the offer rules. The right column costs nothing extra; it only needs a little patience and a test plan written before launch.

a.title: Common mistakes
items: Choosing the shape with most leads
Using lead forms the offer bans

b.title: Fix
items: Same ad, split in the tracker

steps.say: These mistakes come from looking at the wrong number or skipping the offer rules. Read across. Choosing the shape with the most leads? Choose on accepted E P C. Using lead forms the offer bans? Read the funnel rules first. Testing shapes with different ads? Use the same ad, split in the tracker. Deciding after one hundred clicks? Wait for five hundred or more clicks per path. The fixes cost nothing extra, just patience and a written plan.

steps.p: Lead forms inside an ad app send personal data to the advertiser through you or an integration. They need a privacy policy link and clear consent, and the offer must allow them.

d.text: We are not certain which lead form features and fields are current on each platform; check the platform's Help Center. Never use a lead form an offer does not permit.

steps.say: A word on compliance for platform lead forms. These forms, inside an ad app, send personal data to the advertiser through you or an integration. They need a privacy policy link and clear consent, and the offer must allow them. As the warning says, we're not certain which lead form features and fields are current on each platform, so check the platform's Help Center. And never use a lead form an offer doesn't permit.

steps.p: Starting rules to adapt with your own data. Write them in the test plan before the split starts so you cannot move the goalposts afterwards.
d: Compare shapes only after 500+ clicks per path
Keep the challenger only if accepted EPC beats baseline by 10% or more
Any path with accepted rate 15+ points below the other: drop it
Change one thing per test: shape or ad, never both
steps.say: Here are your starting decision rules for funnel shape. Compare shapes only after five hundred or more clicks per path. Keep the challenger only if its accepted E P C beats the baseline by ten percent or more. If any path's accepted rate is fifteen or more points below the other, drop it. And change one thing per test, shape or ad, never both. Write these in your test plan before the split starts, so you can't move the goalposts afterwards.

takeaways: Five common shapes: direct link, prelander, quiz, multi-step, platform lead form.
Compare shapes on accepted EPC; more leads can mean less money.
Split traffic evenly with the same ad and judge after 500+ clicks per path.
lessons.action: For your chosen offer, read its funnel rules and write a one-page test plan: baseline shape, challenger shape, split method, read point (clicks per path) and the decision rule you will apply.

glossary.def: The sequence of pages or steps between the ad click and the conversion.
Sending the ad click straight to the offer's entry page.
A page you control before the offer that explains it and warms the visitor up.
Sending traffic evenly to two versions to compare them fairly.
A form inside the ad app that collects details without leaving it.

quiz.q: Direct: 1,000 clicks, 160 leads, 80% accepted. Prelander: 1,000 clicks, 170 leads, 90% accepted. $1.00 payout. Which has the higher accepted EPC?
The offer page says 'Platform lead forms: not allowed'. A lead form would double your leads. What do you do?
options: Use it on a small budget
Do not use it; pick an allowed shape
Ask users to re-enter on the offer
quiz.why: Funnel rules are part of the offer terms. Breaking them gets leads unpaid.

quiz.q: Challenger EPC $0.21, baseline $0.20 after 600 clicks each. What does the starting rule say?
options: Keep the baseline: the gain is under 10%
quiz.why: $0.21 is only 5% above $0.20. The rule needs 10% or more to switch.

quiz.q: Why test shapes with the same ad?
options: So the shape is the only thing that changed
quiz.why: Change one thing at a time or you cannot tell what caused the result.

quiz.q: Which shape most often brings many leads with a low accepted rate?
options: Platform lead form with pre-filled details
quiz.why: Pre-filled forms are quick to submit without reading, so more get rejected.

lessons.say_intro: This lesson covers funnel shapes for sweepstakes and lead gen. You'll learn the five common shapes, when each one fits, and how to compare them on accepted earnings per click. It matters because the page between the click and the form is where you actually earn.
lessons.say_outro: To recap: there are five common shapes, each offer has rules on which you can use, and you pick the winner on accepted E P C after a fair split, never on lead count. Your task: for your chosen offer, read its funnel rules and write a one-page test plan with your baseline shape, challenger shape, split method, read point in clicks per path, and the decision rule you'll apply. Now take the quiz.

lessons.title: Prelanders that tell the truth
objectives: By the end you can build a prelander with every element an honest sweeps page needs.
By the end you can measure click loss and click-through to the offer, and fix both.
By the end you can run and judge a prelander A/B test with starting rules.

steps.p: A prelander does two jobs: it tells people exactly what they are entering, and it filters out people who would not want to. Done honestly, it lifts the accepted rate. Done with tricks, it inflates leads that get scrubbed and ads that get rejected.

d.b: Explain the draw, then let people choose
d.s: An honest prelander raises accepted EPC.

steps.say: A prelander does two jobs. It tells people exactly what they're entering, and it filters out people who wouldn't want to. Done honestly, it lifts your accepted rate. Done with tricks, it inflates leads that get scrubbed, and ads that get rejected. As the screen says, explain the draw, then let people choose. An honest prelander raises accepted E P C, earnings per click.

steps.p: Six blocks, in this order, on one short mobile page. Every fact comes from the official rules. If a block would need a fact the rules do not give, leave it out.
d: Prize facts|value, number of winners, date
steps.say: Here's the anatomy of an honest prelander: six blocks, in this order, on one short mobile page. A headline with the draw and the prize. Prize facts: value, number of winners and date. How it works, in three short steps. A rules summary: eligibility, free entry and odds. The sponsor, who runs it, with a rules link. And a button that says enter the draw. Every fact comes from the official rules. If a block needs a fact the rules don't give, leave it out.

steps.p: This is what the six blocks look like on a phone. No countdown, no 'you were selected', no fake comments. It is plain, and plain is what keeps the accepted rate high and the ad approved.

page.h: Enter the June $500 gift card draw
page.p: One winner, drawn 1 July. 1) Enter your email. 2) Confirm by email. 3) Wait for the draw. Free, US 18+. Run by Example Rewards Ltd. Official rules linked.

steps.say: Here's what those six blocks look like on a phone. Read it with me. Enter the June five hundred dollar gift card draw. One winner, drawn on the first of July. One, enter your email. Two, confirm by email. Three, wait for the draw. Free, U S adults eighteen plus. Run by Example Rewards Limited, with official rules linked. Notice what's missing: no countdown, no you were selected, no fake comments. Plain is what keeps the accepted rate high and the ad approved.

steps.p: Prelander EPC is the share of visitors who click through to the offer, times what each offer click earns. You can improve either side: a clearer prelander or a better offer page.
steps.more: Example: 64% click through. On the offer, 28% enter and 88% are accepted at $1.20, so each offer click earns 0.28 × 0.88 × $1.20 = $0.296. Prelander EPC = 0.64 × $0.296 = $0.19. That matches the funnel in Lesson 1.
steps.say: Prelander E P C is the share of visitors who click through to the offer, times what each offer click earns. That's the equation on screen. In this example, sixty four percent click through. On the offer, twenty eight percent enter and eighty eight percent are accepted at one dollar twenty, so each offer click earns about thirty cents. Sixty four percent of thirty cents gives a prelander E P C of about nineteen cents. You can improve either side: a clearer prelander, or a better offer page.

steps.p: Click loss is the share of ad clicks that never load your page. Compare clicks in Ads Manager with page views in your tracker. Here 22% of paid clicks never saw the page, usually because it loaded too slowly.

d.label: of paid clicks never reached the page

steps.say: Click loss is the share of ad clicks that never load your page. You find it by comparing clicks in Ads Manager with page views in your tracker. In this example, one thousand clicks led to just seven hundred and eighty page views. So twenty two percent of paid clicks never saw the page, the number on screen. Usually that's because the page loaded too slowly. You paid for those clicks and got nothing.

steps.p: Whatever page builder you use, check these settings. The pulsing one is the button link: it must carry your click ID to the offer, or the network cannot credit you. Setting names here are generic.

blocks.label: Rules link visible above the fold

steps.say: Whatever page builder you use, check these settings. Setting names here are generic. Page weight is three hundred and eighty kilobytes, so aim small. Compress images is on. Now look at the highlighted line, the button link. It must carry your click I D to the offer, or the network can't credit you. Below that, the rules link is visible above the fold. Then publish.

steps.p: You can hand-build prelanders in any page tool. A lander builder made for affiliates can save time on speed, tracking links and mobile layout. Keep every fact from the official rules either way.

d.why: Build fast, mobile-first prelanders with tracking-ready buttons, then fill them only with facts from the rules.

steps.say: You can hand-build prelanders in any page tool. A lander builder made for affiliates, like Landvoo shown here, can save time on speed, tracking links and mobile layout. It's built for fast, mobile-first prelanders with tracking-ready buttons. But either way, fill every page only with facts from the official rules.

steps.p: Example after 600 visits each. B has a slightly lower click-through but a higher accepted rate, because it sets honest expectations. Judge on accepted EPC, which here favours B.
steps.more: A: 0.68 × 0.27 × 0.78 × $1.20 = $0.172. B: 0.64 × 0.28 × 0.88 × $1.20 = $0.189. B wins by about 10%, which meets the starting rule. Example figures; your tests will differ.
steps.say: Here's an example headline test, after six hundred visits each. Headline A says your chance at five hundred dollars. Headline B says enter the June five hundred dollar draw. Read the table. A has a higher click-through, sixty eight percent against sixty four. But B has a higher accepted rate, eighty eight percent against seventy eight, because it sets honest expectations. So B wins on accepted E P C, nineteen cents against seventeen, about ten percent better. These are example figures.

steps.p: Start every prelander from this skeleton and fill each line from the official rules. If you cannot fill a line truthfully, delete it rather than inventing something.

d.text:
Headline: Enter the [month] [prize] draw
Prize: [prize], [number] winner(s), drawn [date]
How it works: 1) [entry step] 2) [confirm step] 3) [draw]
Small print: Free to enter. [eligibility]. Odds depend on entries.
Sponsor: [legal name]. Official rules: [link]
Button: Enter the draw

steps.say: Start every prelander from this copy skeleton, the text on screen. It has a line for the headline, the prize, how it works in three steps, the small print saying it's free, the eligibility and that odds depend on entries, the sponsor with a rules link, and the button. Fill each line from the official rules. If you can't fill a line truthfully, delete it rather than inventing something.

steps.p: The left column raises clicks for a day and lowers payouts for a month. Several also break platform policies on misleading content and fake endorsements.

b.title: Fix
items: Compress, aim for a light page

steps.say: These mistakes raise clicks for a day and lower payouts for a month. Several also break platform policies on misleading content and fake endorsements. Read across. A fake news-article layout? Use a plain page that's clearly an ad. Fake comments or winners? Only real, permitted info. A countdown that resets? Use the real closing date from the rules. Heavy images and slow load? Compress, and aim for a light page.

steps.h: Compliance: no fake formats or endorsements
steps.p: Prelanders styled as news articles, invented comments, fake winner photos and celebrity images without permission are misleading and break most platforms' policies and consumer law.

d.text: Never imply endorsement, editorial coverage or winners that do not exist. Every claim on the page must come from the official rules.

steps.say: Compliance matters here. Prelanders styled as news articles, invented comments, fake winner photos, and celebrity images without permission are misleading. They break most platforms' policies and consumer law. As the warning says, never imply endorsement, editorial coverage, or winners that don't exist. Every claim on the page must come from the official rules.

steps.p: Starting rules to adapt. Check click loss and click-through daily in the first week, and judge A/B tests only at the read point you wrote before launch.
d: Click loss over 20%: fix page speed before anything else
Click-through under 40% after 300 visits: rewrite the page
Judge A/B tests after 500+ visits per version
Keep a variant only if accepted EPC beats the other by 10% or more
steps.say: Here are starting decision rules for prelanders. If click loss is over twenty percent, fix page speed before anything else. If click-through is under forty percent after three hundred visits, rewrite the page. Judge A B tests only after five hundred or more visits per version. And keep a variant only if its accepted E P C beats the other by ten percent or more. Check click loss and click-through daily in the first week.

takeaways: An honest prelander has six blocks, all taken from the official rules.
Prelander EPC = click-through × offer EPC; click loss tells you if speed is costing you.
Judge prelander tests on accepted EPC after 500+ visits per version.

quiz.q: Click-through 50%, offer EPC $0.30. What is prelander EPC?
Ads Manager shows 1,200 clicks; your tracker shows 840 page views. What is the click loss and the action?
quiz.why: 1 − 840 ÷ 1,200 = 30%, above the 20% line. Speed is usually the cause.

quiz.q: Which prelander element is allowed?
options: A countdown that resets every visit
A rules summary with a link to the full rules
quiz.why: A rules summary is honest and helps people decide. The others are misleading.

quiz.q: Version A: 70% click-through, 75% accepted. Version B: 62%, 90% accepted. Same 28% form rate and payout. Which wins on accepted EPC?
quiz.why: A: 0.70 × 0.75 = 0.525. B: 0.62 × 0.90 = 0.558. B earns about 6% more per visit, though under the 10% rule you would keep testing.

quiz.q: Where should every fact on your prelander come from?
quiz.why: Your page can only promise what the rules promise.

lessons.say_intro: In this lesson you'll build prelanders that tell the truth. You'll learn the six blocks of an honest page, how to measure click loss and click-through, and how to judge a headline test. It matters because an honest prelander raises your accepted earnings, while tricks get leads scrubbed and ads rejected.

Now take the quiz.

lessons.title: Quizzes and surveys without the tricks
objectives: By the end you can design a short quiz that personalises the next step without implying a win.
By the end you can measure quiz completion and its effect on accepted EPC.
By the end you know which questions you should never ask in a sweeps quiz.

steps.p: Quizzes are popular in sweeps because tapping answers feels easy. The risk is the result screen. 'Congratulations, you qualify' turns a harmless quiz into a misleading promise. Built honestly, a quiz helps people pick what they want and lifts quality.

d.b: A quiz may personalise, never promise
d.s: The result screen is where most quizzes break the rules.

steps.say: Quizzes are popular in sweeps, because tapping answers feels easy. The risk is the result screen. Congratulations, you qualify, turns a harmless quiz into a misleading promise. Built honestly, a quiz helps people pick what they want, and it lifts quality. As the screen says, a quiz may personalise, but never promise.

steps.p: Keep it short. Each question must have a purpose the person can see, such as choosing a prize type or a topic for emails. The result explains what happens next, nothing more.
steps.say: Here's the structure of an honest quiz. Follow the flow. One easy opening question. Then two or three purposeful questions. Then an honest summary of choices, the entry button, and the official rules link. Keep it short. Each question must have a purpose the person can see, like choosing a prize type or a topic for emails. The result explains what happens next, and nothing more.

steps.h: Example: a quiz in a chat-style flow
steps.p: Example quiz on a phone. The questions shape which draw and which emails the person sees. The last message tells them what entering means. Nothing says they have won or qualified.

messages.text: Which gift card would you rather enter a draw for?
How often would you like deal emails?
Thanks. You can enter the June $500 grocery card draw. Free, one winner, rules linked. Entering means weekly deal emails.

steps.say: Here's an example quiz in a chat-style flow on a phone. First it asks which gift card you'd rather enter a draw for, and the person picks groceries. Then it asks how often you'd like deal emails, and they pick weekly. The last message says thanks, you can enter the June five hundred dollar grocery card draw. Free, one winner, rules linked, and entering means weekly deal emails. Notice that nothing says they've won or qualified.

steps.p: The result screen decides whether the quiz is honest. The left side implies a win or special status. The right side summarises choices and explains the entry.
steps.say: The result screen decides whether the quiz is honest. On the left, misleading lines: congratulations, you qualify. You're one of five selected. Your prize is reserved. Only two spots left for you. These imply a win or special status. On the right, honest lines: thanks, here's your draw. You chose a grocery card. Enter free, rules linked. The draw closes thirtieth June. These just summarise choices and explain the entry.

steps.p: Example, 1,000 clicks. 85% start, 70% finish, 62% tap through to the entry form, and 29% of those enter. That gives 180 leads. The question is whether they are accepted at a higher rate than your plain prelander's leads.
steps.say: Here's an example quiz funnel from one thousand clicks. Follow the bars down. Eight hundred and fifty start the quiz, seven hundred finish, six hundred and twenty reach the entry form, and one hundred and eighty enter. That's one hundred and eighty leads. But the real question is whether they're accepted at a higher rate than your plain prelander's leads.

steps.h: Example: completion by number of questions
steps.p: Example from one test. Each extra question loses some people. Seven questions finished at 55%, four at 70%. Only add a question if its answer changes something for the person.
steps.say: Every extra question loses some people. In this example from one test, look at the bars. Three questions finished at seventy four percent. Four, at seventy percent. Five, at sixty four. And seven questions, only fifty five percent. So only add a question if its answer changes something for the person.

steps.h: Example: is the quiz worth it?
steps.p: Example: 180 leads × 90% accepted × $1.20 = $194.40 per 1,000 clicks, EPC $0.19. The plain prelander earned $188.40, EPC $0.19. Only about 3% better, so under the 10% rule the quiz has not earned its place yet.
steps.say: So, is the quiz worth it? In this example, one hundred and eighty leads, times ninety percent accepted, times one dollar twenty, gives one hundred and ninety four dollars forty per thousand clicks. That's an E P C, earnings per click, of nineteen cents. The plain prelander earned one hundred and eighty eight dollars forty, also about nineteen cents. The quiz is only about three percent better, so under the ten percent rule, it hasn't earned its place yet.

steps.p: Check these settings in whatever quiz tool you use. The pulsing one is the result text: write it last, from the official rules, and read it as if you were a tired person on a bus.

blocks.label: Result text
blocks.value: Thanks. You can enter the June $500 grocery card draw. Rules linked.

steps.say: Check these settings in whatever quiz tool you use. In this example there are three questions, and answers are saved with a consent record. Look at the highlighted line, the result text. It reads: thanks, you can enter the June five hundred dollar grocery card draw, rules linked. Write it last, from the official rules, and read it as if you were a tired person on a bus. The rules link is also shown on the result.

steps.p: Quiz answers are personal data. Some are sensitive data under many laws. Unless an offer lawfully needs one and the person clearly agrees, leave these out of sweeps quizzes.
d: Anything not used|collect only what you need
steps.say: Quiz answers are personal data, and some are sensitive data under many laws. Look at the cards. Health conditions are sensitive data. Debts or income are financial details. Religion or politics are sensitive data. A child's age is minors' data. And anything you won't use, don't collect. Unless an offer lawfully needs one of these and the person clearly agrees, leave them out of sweeps quizzes.

steps.p: Most broken quizzes were built to raise click-through, not to help the person. Every question and every result line should pass a simple test: would you be happy to explain it to a regulator?
d: Seven questions for nothing|cut to what changes the next step
steps.say: Most broken quizzes were built to raise click-through, not to help the person. Look at the fixes. You qualify results? Summarise choices instead. Seven questions for nothing? Cut to what changes the next step. Fake progress bars? Show real steps. Sensitive questions? Leave them out. Every question and result line should pass a simple test: would you be happy to explain it to a regulator?

steps.p: Quiz answers become personal data once they are linked to an email. Collect only what you need, explain why you ask, and store the answers with the consent record so you can show what was agreed.

d.text: Never imply eligibility, selection or a reserved prize. Avoid sensitive questions such as health, finances or religion unless an offer lawfully needs them with explicit consent.

steps.say: Quiz answers become personal data once they're linked to an email. So collect only what you need, explain why you ask, and store answers with the consent record, so you can show what was agreed. As the warning says, never imply eligibility, selection or a reserved prize. And avoid sensitive questions like health, finances or religion, unless an offer lawfully needs them with explicit consent.

A quiz is extra work and extra data to protect, so it has to earn its place.

takeaways: A quiz may personalise the next step; it must never imply a win or selection.

lessons.title: DOI confirmation: helping real people confirm
objectives: By the end you can map every step between an SOI and a confirmed DOI.
By the end you can work out what a higher confirm rate is worth.
By the end you can test your own DOI flow and apply confirm-rate rules.

steps.p: On a DOI offer, the confirm rate decides your value per raw lead more than almost anything else. People who meant to enter still miss emails, find them in spam or forget. Small, honest fixes to the confirmation journey can lift your earnings without spending more on ads.

d.b: Confirms are earned after the form
d.s: Help people who meant to enter finish.

steps.say: On a D O I, double opt-in, offer, the confirm rate decides your value per raw lead more than almost anything else. People who meant to enter still miss emails, find them in spam, or simply forget. As the screen says, confirms are earned after the form. Help people who meant to enter finish. Small, honest fixes to this journey can lift your earnings without spending more on ads.

steps.p: Each step loses some people. You control some steps, the advertiser controls others. Know which is which so you ask the right person to fix the right problem.
steps.say: Follow the flow from S O I, single opt-in, to a confirmed D O I. The form is submitted. A thank-you page explains the next step. An email or S M S arrives. The person taps confirm. They see a confirmed page. And the D O I postback fires. Each step loses some people. You control some steps, and the advertiser controls others. Know which is which, so you ask the right person to fix the right problem.

steps.p: The thank-you page should say exactly what to do next: which inbox, which sender, what subject line, and to check spam. Many people stop here because nothing tells them a second step exists.

page.h: One more step: confirm your entry
page.p: We sent an email from draws@example-rewards.example with the subject 'Confirm your June draw entry'. Not there in 2 minutes? Check spam or promotions.

steps.say: Here's a thank-you page that helps. The heading says one more step: confirm your entry. Then it tells people exactly what to look for: which sender the email comes from, shown on screen, and the subject line, confirm your June draw entry. And if it's not there in two minutes, check spam or promotions. The button opens the email app. Many people stop at this point simply because nothing tells them a second step exists.

steps.p: Some DOI offers confirm by SMS. The message names the sender, says what replying means and how to stop. Example only; SMS rules are strict in many geos, especially the US.

The person replies yes, and gets a thanks, you're entered, draw on the first of July, reply stop any time. This is an example only. S M S rules are strict in many geos, especially the U S.

steps.h: Example: what a better confirm rate is worth
steps.p: Example: DOI $2.50, 97% accepted. A clearer thank-you page lifts confirms from 38% to 46%. Value per raw lead rises from $0.92 to $1.12. On 1,000 raw leads that is about $194 more, with no extra ad spend.
steps.more: Exact: 2.50 × 0.46 × 0.97 = 1.1155. 2.50 × 0.38 × 0.97 = 0.9215. Difference 0.194, so about $194 per 1,000 raw leads. Example figures; test on your own offer.
steps.say: What's a better confirm rate worth? In this example, the D O I pays two dollars fifty, with ninety seven percent accepted. A clearer thank-you page lifts confirms from thirty eight percent to forty six. Follow the equation. Value per raw lead rises from about ninety two cents to one dollar twelve, about nineteen cents more. On one thousand raw leads, that's about one hundred and ninety four dollars more, with no extra ad spend. Test this on your own offer.

Reminders are the advertiser's decision, but you can ask whether they send one.

steps.say: If the wiring is wrong, you either can't see which ads make money, or the network can't credit you at all. Both are expensive. steps.p: The click goes out with IDs attached. The conversion comes back with the same IDs. Your tracker joins them up and can send the event on to the ad platform. Each arrow must carry the click ID.

The lead goes to the network. The network sends back an S O I or D O I postback, single or double opt-in, with the click I D and event. The tracker matches it, and can send a server event on to the ad platform. Every arrow must carry the click I D.

steps.say: If the offer lets you host the form, you send each lead to the advertiser's A P I, with consent details attached. The example on screen uses dummy data, so I won't read it. Notice what it includes: the offer, the click I D, the email, the exact consent text, a timestamp, the page version and the I P address. Only do this when the offer permits it, over H T T P S, with the consent record included, and follow the advertiser's A P I docs.

steps.say: Here's how to test the whole wiring. Run it before every launch and after any change, and use test mode or tell the manager, so test leads aren't paid. Tap Next to follow each step. First, click your own ad link, the live one with sub I Ds, on a phone. Second, check the click shows in the tracker within a minute, with its sub I Ds. Third, submit a test lead and confirm the S O I postback arrives against that click I D. Fourth, tap the confirm link and check the D O I postback. Fifth, check the network report shows the test under the right sub I D.

steps.p: Example: compare tracker and network counts daily. A gap that matches the usual scrub is normal. A sudden gap, or zero, usually means broken wiring, not bad traffic.
steps.say: Compare tracker and network counts every day. In this example, read the table. Monday, one hundred and eighty tracker leads and one hundred and fifty three on the network, a normal fifteen percent scrub. Tuesday, also normal. Wednesday, one hundred and ninety in the tracker, but zero on the network. That's a broken postback. Thursday, about half are missing, so check it. A gap that matches the usual scrub is normal. A sudden gap or a zero usually means broken wiring, not bad traffic.

steps.p: Follow this order on launch day. Each step depends on the one before it, and skipping ahead is how most blind spending starts. Keep the first hour's budget small until the first postback arrives.
d: Check first postback within the hour
steps.say: Follow this order on launch day, because each step depends on the one before. Build links with sub I Ds. Run the wiring test. Launch at a low budget. Check the first postback arrives within the hour. Then have your first checkpoint the next day. Keep the first hour's budget small until that first postback arrives. Skipping ahead is how most blind spending starts.

steps.say: Almost every one of these mistakes is caught by the walkthrough test. One link for every ad set? Use sub I Ds from platform macros. No D O I postback? Set up separate S O I and D O I postbacks. Testing on desktop only? Test on a phone, with the live link. Personal data in sub I Ds? Use I Ds only, never personal data. Teams that skip the test usually find these after a week of blind spending.

steps.p: Sub IDs and URLs are logged by many systems. Personal data must never travel in them. Sending lead data to ad platforms has its own rules on hashing and consent.

d.text: Never put emails, names or phone numbers in URLs or sub IDs. Only send customer data to an ad platform when the person's consent and the platform's current terms allow it.

steps.say: Now compliance, on personal data in tracking. Sub I Ds and links are logged by many systems, so personal data must never travel in them. Sending lead data to ad platforms has its own rules on hashing and consent. As the warning says, never put emails, names or phone numbers in links or sub I Ds. Only send customer data to an ad platform when the person's consent and the platform's current terms allow it.

steps.p: Starting rules to adapt. They catch broken wiring within hours instead of days, which is the difference between a small loss and a large one.
d: Run the full wiring test before every launch
Tracker vs network gap more than 10 points above normal scrub: investigate
Zero postbacks for 2 × the usual time between leads: pause and test
Never scale until the network report matches the tracker within normal scrub
steps.say: Here are your starting rules for tracking. Run the full wiring test before every launch. If the tracker and network gap is more than ten points above your normal scrub, investigate. If there are zero postbacks for twice the usual time between leads, pause and test. And never scale until the network report matches the tracker within normal scrub. These catch broken wiring within hours instead of days, which is the difference between a small loss and a large one.

takeaways: Put sub IDs on every link and get separate SOI and DOI postbacks.
Test the whole wiring on a phone with a test lead before every launch.
Compare tracker and network counts daily; a sudden gap means broken wiring.

glossary.def: A placeholder in an ad URL that the platform fills in, such as the ad set ID. Also called a macro.
A unique ID your tracker gives each click so conversions can be matched to it.
A server-to-server call from the network to your tracker when a conversion happens.
Sending a lead you collected to the advertiser's system through an API.
A network setting that marks conversions as tests so they are not paid.

quiz.q: Tracker shows 200 leads, network shows 0 today, yesterday it showed 85% of tracker. What is most likely?
quiz.why: A sudden drop to zero usually means wiring, not quality. Run the wiring test.

quiz.q: Why ask for separate SOI and DOI postbacks?
options: To see the confirm rate per ad set
quiz.why: With both events you can see which ad sets bring people who confirm.

quiz.q: Which sub ID value is acceptable?
quiz.why: IDs only. Personal data must never travel in URLs or sub IDs.

quiz.q: Normal scrub is 15%. Today the network shows 60% of tracker leads. What does the starting rule say?
options: Investigate: the gap is far more than 10 points above normal
quiz.why: A 40% gap is 25 points above normal scrub, past the investigate line.

quiz.q: When should you run the full wiring test?
options: Before every launch and after any change
quiz.why: Most tracking breaks after a change to links, pages or offers.

lessons.say_intro: This lesson is about wiring the whole flow: sub I Ds, postbacks and lead posting. You'll build a tracking link and postbacks for single and double opt-in, test the wiring with a test lead before launch, and spot broken tracking from the numbers. It matters because broken tracking turns every decision into a guess.
lessons.say_outro: To recap: every arrow must carry the click I D, use separate S O I and D O I postbacks, never put personal data in links, and run the full wiring test before every launch. Your task: build your tracking link with sub I Ds, set up S O I and D O I postbacks for your chosen offer, run the five-step wiring test, and screenshot each step into your compliance file. Now take the quiz.

exam.q: Path A (direct): 1,000 clicks, 170 leads, 80% accepted. Path B (prelander): 1,000 clicks, 160 leads, 92% accepted. $1.20 payout. What do you do?
options: Keep testing; B is about 8% better, under the 10% rule
exam.why: A: 170 × 0.80 × 1.20 = $163.20. B: 160 × 0.92 × 1.20 = $176.64, about 8% more. Under 10%, keep testing to more clicks.

exam.q: Ads Manager shows 2,000 clicks; your tracker shows 1,500 prelander views. What do you fix first?
options: Page speed: 25% click loss is above 20%

exam.q: A quiz result says 'Congratulations, you qualify for the $500 prize'. The draw is random. What is wrong?
options: It implies eligibility or a win that does not exist
exam.why: A random draw has no qualifying. The result must summarise choices and explain entry.

exam.q: Quiz EPC $0.23, plain prelander $0.20, after 700 clicks each, accepted rates similar. Keep the quiz?
Invalid-lead rate 9% on 500 leads at $1.10. How much is lost, and what is the rule?
DOI $2.80, 95% accepted. A thank-you page fix lifts confirms from 36% to 44%. Extra per 1,000 raw leads?
Confirm rate is 26% on 140 raw leads, 80 hours after launch. What does the starting rule say?
options: Pause and test the DOI flow
exam.why: Under 30% on 100+ raw leads after 72 hours: pause and test.

exam.q: A colleague wants to add the lead's email to sub3 'to match leads easily'. What do you say?
options: Hash it first in the URL
No: never put personal data in URLs or sub IDs; use the click ID
exam.why: The click ID already matches leads. Personal data in URLs is logged widely and breaks data rules.

exam.q: Tracker 210 leads, network 0, for 6 hours. Leads usually arrive every few minutes. What do you do?
options: Pause and run the wiring test
exam.why: Zero postbacks for far longer than twice the usual gap means broken wiring.

exam.q: The offer allows prelanders but not platform lead forms. A lead form would double raw leads. What do you do?
options: Use the lead form on a second account
Use an allowed shape and improve the prelander instead
Ask entrants to re-enter on the offer page
exam.why: Offer funnel rules are terms. Break them and leads go unpaid.
